claims.text: Powder precursors may be prepared by mechanical alloying or homogeneous mixing before sintering.
Such metallic or ceramic powder precursors conventionally require high-temperature sintering for densification.
A machine-learning model can use experimental and simulation data to predict optimum sintering parameters.
Machine-learning optimization can prescribe a lower-temperature sintering regime.
Relevant optimization variables include particle-size distribution, heating rate, pressure, and additive dosage.
Powder processing and sintering can be conducted under a controlled inert atmosphere.
The proposed approach requires systematic variation of heating rate, applied pressure, and sintering-aid use.
Starting powders can be homogeneously blended before sintering.
Optimized sintering parameters enhance mass transport along activated diffusion pathways at lower temperatures.
Optimized lower-temperature sintering minimizes grain coarsening.
Optimized lower-temperature sintering limits deleterious phase formation.
Machine learning can uncover nonlinear relationships between process variables and densification outcomes.
Adjustment of sintering conditions identified by machine learning can make lower temperatures sufficient for full or near-full densification.
The proposed method will significantly reduce the required sintering temperature relative to conventional sintering.
Lower-temperature, machine-learning-optimized sintering will achieve density and microstructural quality comparable to conventional sintering.
The resulting microstructure will maintain desired mechanical and functional properties.
Conventional high-temperature sintering can be energy intensive and can degrade microstructural features.
The approach may be limited by complex phase equilibria, insufficient training data, powder characteristics, and processing environment.
The magnitude and cross-system universality of the temperature reduction are uncertain pending experimental validation.
Failure of the lower-temperature protocol to match the conventional protocol in densification, phase purity, and mechanical properties would falsify the hypothesis.
